item.title: Research with Impact: Qualitative approaches to social and behaviour change
item.content:encoded:
This special issue seeks to demonstrate how qualitative and interpretive research can drive meaningful social and behavioural change, particularly for underrepresented and marginalised groups. Rather than relying solely on quantitative metrics, the collection aims to show how deep qualitative inquiry uncovers the psychological and cultural factors that shape human behaviour and can inform ethical, inclusive interventions that address complex social problems.

The call reflects growing recognition that qualitative research must evolve to engage participatory and inclusive frameworks, especially when working with neurodivergent, trauma-affected, and marginalised populations. The special issue responds to an urgent need for research methodologies that empower rather than merely study neglected communities, drawing on approaches such as netnography and community-led participatory methods to create transformative social impact.

Appel publié par Qualitative Market Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Present innovative qualitative approaches to design and/or evaluate social marketing initiatives
  • Develop qualitative approaches for inclusive research
  • Describe participatory approaches (e.g. action research, co-design)
  • Engage with difficult, sensitive, or stigmatised topics, developing sensemaking through qualitative methods
  • Reflect on the ethics of participatory inclusive methods for behaviour and social change
  • Develop longitudinal qualitative frameworks to demonstrate the social impact of ethical interventions and inclusive social marketing strategies

Timeline

  • January 10, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • December 15, 2026: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Persuasive Technology 2026
item.content:encoded:
Elena Vlahu Gjorgievska, University of Wollongong

Kiemute Oyibo, York University

Yugo Nakamura, Ritsumeikan University

The special issue will include selected papers from the 21st International Conference on Persuasive Technology. The special issue will be by invitation only.

This special issue is by invitation only. Invited papers must have at least 35% extra content from the conference paper. The additional content cannot be related work only or an extended discussion, but should include at least 35% of new results.

item.title: Social Marketing and Sustainable Futures
item.content:encoded:
Social marketing has long been positioned as a discipline capable of improving societal wellbeing by applying marketing principles to influence behaviour in socially beneficial ways. Early contributions that imagined marketing being used beyond the commercial realm laid the foundation for the field's formal emergence in the early 1970s. Over the decades, social marketing has advanced its understanding of how to encourage and sustain behaviour change, yet the contemporary landscape presents challenges of a fundamentally different scale.

Increasing environmental degradation, climate instability, resource pressures, and persistent social inequities highlight the need for social marketing approaches capable of addressing system-wide issues. While behaviour remains a central concern, scholars have argued that meaningful progress requires attention to macro-level structures and the dynamic interactions among actors, networks, institutions, and infrastructures. Social marketing is therefore being called upon not merely to promote individual behaviour change, but to support the creation of sustainable futures through coordinated, multi-level forms of change.

Appel publié par European Journal of Marketing. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

  • Critical reviews of social marketing's development and its relevance to sustainability

  • Community-based social marketing and collective approaches to sustainable behaviour change
